decision: Qualify TQP-43 for the retained Windows fault-order determinism and fail-closed recovery profile.
alternatives_considered: treat one successful native run as sufficient determinism evidence
simulate native allocation and publication failures only in GDScript
compare history-dependent resident caches without a viewer lifecycle barrier
accept an empty final mesh because active records were present
claim arbitrary operating-system out-of-memory recovery from explicit failpoints
evidence: matching debug and release native fault-order authority hashes across 64 deterministic completion-order shuffles
15 retained Windows debug process runs pinned by upstream commit, executable hash, native hash, fixed counters, duration distribution, and peak working set
native cancellation/replacement, duplicate and stale completion, two allocation admission failures, interrupted publication, malformed output and descriptor, recovery, and clean shutdown controls
generation-aware negative-control trace reporting first divergent generation 4
three rapid-viewer histories with a proven zero-resource lifecycle drain followed by one canonical final demand
identical non-empty state and geometry signatures with 22 authoritative render resources after every history
asynchronous stale viewer revision rejection and coalesced supersession events
@tool Fault-Order Determinism Observatory with retained storm and forward-versus-reverse validation
qualified_scope: Windows native debug/release deterministic fault-order authority for the retained eight-record corpus
explicit page-buffer and snapshot-workspace allocation admission failures with declared recovery
interrupted publication and malformed output/descriptor fail-closed controls
bounded Windows debug Godot rapid-motion convergence after a complete viewer lifecycle drain
non-empty active-state and mesh identity, stale revision rejection, and clean shutdown
reference-only process duration and Windows peak-working-set evidence
unqualified_scope: arbitrary operating-system out-of-memory recovery or exception-based allocation failure
exhaustive thread schedules, hardware faults, disk exhaustion, concurrent process writers, or power loss
history-independent resident cache policy before a lifecycle drain
human visual acceptance, multi-hour soak, production frame pacing, low-power targets, networking, GPU authority, Gate E, or production terrain
review: Qualification fails closed if provenance, native hash or counters, retained runs, declared fault outcomes, first divergent generation, lifecycle drain, non-empty state/geometry identity, stale rejection, observatory workflow, or explicit limitations differ.
downstream_impact: TQP-44 becomes the next dependency-ordered milestone and requires human visual and temporal review. Gate E remains closed.
